add.title: CeCe McDonald (Wikipedia; Minnesota prisoner-placement case)
add.summary: Documented Minnesota DOC placement practice, birth-sex determined: CeCe McDonald, a transgender woman, pleaded guilty to second-degree manslaughter and was sentenced on 4 June 2012 to 41 months; her attorneys acknowledged there was 'no way' she would be sent to a women's prison and 'really no history of transgender people being placed according to their gender identity'. The Minnesota Department of Corrections placed her in an adult male facility, Minnesota Correctional Facility - St. Cloud, after a state gender assessment concluded she would be held in a men's facility; despite a later transfer to a second facility she remained quartered with men throughout her imprisonment (a petition during her imprisonment led DOC to administer the correct hormone regimen). She was held in segregated custody while awaiting trial, and in May 2012 a fellow inmate attacked her with a glass, causing a wound requiring eleven stitches; the attacker pleaded guilty in April 2013 to third-degree assault and received six months' jail time plus probation.
